title: Round about Armenia
subtitle: The Record of a Journey across the Balkans through Turkey, the Caucasus, and Persia in 1895

divisions.title: The book’s title above Chapter I

summary: E. A. Brayley Hodgetts, a correspondent of the London Daily Graphic, set out in January 1895 to look into the reports of massacres of Armenians in the Ottoman Empire. He went by Sofia to Constantinople, along the Black Sea to Trebizond and Batoum, to Tiflis and Baku, across the Caspian to Resht, on horseback to Tabreez, back by Erivan and Etchmiadzin, and along the Russian shores of the Black Sea. The book, written in 1896 after the later massacres, mixes the journey with chapters on the Sassun massacres of 1894, the economy of Turkish Armenia, Armenian parties in Russia, and the Armenian question, and quotes newspapers and his own letters at length. A folding map shows his route.
